builder_plan.scenario: An agent looks good in demos, but you cannot tell which product tasks it fails.
builder_plan.change: Use the study's evaluation idea to inspect a small set of tasks with human-checked answers.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current evaluator and a manually reviewed reference set.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Agreement with human review, missed failures, false alarms, and evaluation cost per task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Inference after coding agents
summary: The method replaces uncorrected classical inference after agent-driven data analysis with a post-hoc replay procedure: reset the agent on subsamples of the data to estimate the probability it would select the reported analysis when it is statistically favorable, then adjust the test conditional on selection. The cost is substantial additional agent compute (multiple black-box replays per analysis, which scales with API or GPU budget) plus engineering to snapshot and replay the exact agent environment; statistical validity requires that the agent's selection behavior be stable across replays. It can fail if the agent's behavior is non-deterministic, drifts between runs, depends on unreplayable state, or if the subsample design does not approximate the original selection process; nominal coverage is only guaranteed asymptotically and conditional on stable selection.
rationale: Any team using coding agents for empirical or data-analysis decisions faces a demonstrated selective-inference risk, and this correction is the first tool that addresses it without modeling the agent's internals, but its replay cost and stability assumptions require workload-specific validation before production adoption.
technique: Replay-based selective-inference correction for coding agents

claims.statement: The method replaces uncorrected classical inference after agent-driven data analysis with a post-hoc replay procedure: reset the agent on subsamples of the data to estimate the probability it would select the reported analysis when it is statistically favorable, then adjust the test conditional on selection. The cost is substantial additional agent compute (multiple black-box replays per analysis, which scales with API or GPU budget) plus engineering to snapshot and replay the exact agent environment; statistical validity requires that the agent's selection behavior be stable across replays. It can fail if the agent's behavior is non-deterministic, drifts between runs, depends on unreplayable state, or if the subsample design does not approximate the original selection process; nominal coverage is only guaranteed asymptotically and conditional on stable selection.
Uncorrected frontier agents report significant p-values on null data 54-98% of the time; the proposed replay correction lowers false rejection rates to near the nominal 5% in simulations.
